title: Introduce cost-weighted-trace-sampling-and-adaptive-log-throttle-for-kv-heavy-paths
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: signal from heavy inference requests (long sequences, large embedding batches, cache-miss retries) drives most observability cost and also contains the highest value for debugging and cost attribution. The current uniform sampling of traces loses signal on those high-cost, low-frequency requests and produces noisy cost estimates per-customer and per-route. This PR implements a cost-weighted trace sampling strategy plus an adaptive log throttling subsystem to reduce log volume from noisy internal retries and bulk telemetry during KV-cache warmups.

What this does (summary): adds a new sampling layer in the runtime request pipeline that computes an inexpensive token-cost estimate and biases sampling probability by cost (configurable power-law weight). Adds an on-path early-suppression filter for verbose logs and an adaptive token-aware throttle that temporarily reduces structured log emission during controlled bursts (e.g., cache-warm). Introduces a calibration job that replays a reservoir of sampled requests offline to correct sampling bias and provide unbiased aggregated metrics. Adds a Grafana dashboard (Token Spend Ledger) that shows per-cluster/per-model token spend waterfall, sampled trace contribution, and an estimator for unsampled spend.

Implementation notes: sampling lives in runtime/sampler with a simple SDK-compatible interface so Dedicated and Private runtimes can opt-in. Sampling decision: P(sample) = min(1, alpha * cost^beta) where cost is token_estimate + kv_retry_penalty. Beta defaults to 0.75; alpha is auto-calibrated based on target sample rate. The offline calibration job computes Horvitz-Thompson estimators to produce unbiased sums for cost/latency and exposes correction weights to dashboards. The adaptive log throttle tracks per-node recent token throughput and reduces structured log rate for tracer/span-level logs (preserves error/warn).

Testing and validation: unit tests for sampling math and edge cases added. End-to-end integration in staging with a synthetic KV-cache-heavy workload (500k requests over 24h) showed: ~62% reduction in log throughput, 48% lower cost for observability pipeline, and 2.3x increase in high-cost trace capture (top 99.9th token spend). Calibration offline job reduced estimation error on cumulative spend from 14% to under 3% in tests.

Rollout plan: staged rollout: 1) merge to main gated by canary job, 2) enable sampling in telemetry namespace in staging for 48h, 3) enable alpha config for 5% of production traffic with read-only dashboards, 4) ramp to target over 72h while monitoring sampler_utilization and sampled_bias metrics.

Backward compatibility: defaults keep behavior identical (alpha=0) until ops flips a feature flag. Operators can tune alpha/beta/target_sample_rate via Helm values and the Console feature flag.

Notes: this changes observability economics but intentionally avoids removing any error-level logs. The PR contains fast paths for Private installs to use KMS-encrypted reservoirs (notes in docs).

review_threads:
Diego Morales: Can you explain how alpha is calibrated automatically?
Aisha: Added a short section in the docs and implemented an autoscaler that keeps expected sample rate near target by adjusting alpha every minute using recent token throughput estimates.

Priya Singh: Concerned about bias introduced for latency percentiles.
Aisha: Offline calibration computes Horvitz-Thompson weights and we expose corrected percentiles in the dashboard. Added unit tests and integration check in staging to validate 99th/99.9th latency with correction applied.

Evan Cho: Will this increase load on trace storage due to more heavy traces?
Aisha: Yes but net storage decreased because we sample more heavy requests but aggressively throttle verbose logs; also the offline estimator reduces the need for storing full raw traces for all requests. Added throttling thresholds configurable per-tenant.
release_notes: Adds cost-weighted trace sampling and adaptive log throttling to reduce observability costs while improving capture of high-cost requests. New Grafana Token Spend Ledger and calibration job enable unbiased cost estimates from sampled traces. Configurable via Helm and Console feature flag.
test_plan: Run CI (unit + integration). Deploy to staging with synthetic KV-heavy workload for 48h, validate sampled_bias < 5% and estimator error < 3%. Canary 5% production traffic then ramp with monitoring. Manual smoke test for console feature flag toggles.
rollout: stage-1: enable in staging namespace for 48h
stage-2: enable for 5% prod traffic with read-only dashboards
stage-3: monitor for 72h and ramp to target if metrics stable
stage-4: document config knobs and hand off to SRE
rationale: Improves debugging signal for costly requests and reduces long-term observability spend by emphasizing higher-value traces and suppressing noisy log bursts.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag default is off. Helm values: telemetry.sampler.enabled, telemetry.sampler.alpha, telemetry.sampler.beta, telemetry.throttle.tokens_window_ms. Private installs should enable sampler.reservoir_kms_key to use encrypted reservoirs. Monitor sampler.sampled_rate and sampler.bias_correction_error during rollout.
